title: European Markets Set to Fall at Open Following U.S. and Asian Markets Down
text:
European Markets Set to Fall at Open Following U.S. and Asian Markets Down U.S. markets are expected to open marginally higher on Tuesday after Monday's selloff By Lisa Botter Apr3,20182:41AMEDT 
European markets looked set to open lower on Tuesday, April 4, after a long holiday weekend following Asian markets down after U.S. stocks plummeted on Monday. 
FTSE 100 futures at 7:18 am in London were pointing to a more than 1% drop at open. Germany's Dax is expected to fall 1.05% and France's CAC 40 was marked 0.6% lower. 
U.S. markets are expected to open marginally up on Tuesday after Monday's selloff that marked the worst start to April since the Great Depression, according to Bloomberg. S&P 500 mini futures were 0.27% higher at 2:20 am EST. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was 0.07% higher and Nasdaq mini futures were up 0.27%. 
Wall Street was hard hit on Monday , dragged down by technology stocks. The S&P 500 lost 2.23% at 2,581.88, entering correction territory. The Nasdaq Composite also entered correction territory, losing 2.74%. 
The index was pulled down by Intel Corp. ( INTC ) , which lost more than 6% on reports that Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) would bring chipmaking in-house from 2020. 
Amazon Inc. ( AMZN ) lost more than 5% on an attack from President Donald Trump on Twiiter that the e-commerce giant was forcing the U.S. Postal Service to make deliveries at a loss. 
Asia's equity markets were lower Tuesday, taking a cue from losses on Wall Street. Worries about an impending trade war between the U.S. and China also sent ripples through the markets. 
Japan's Nikkei lost 0.45% to 21,292, and the Topix was down 0.29%. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng lost 0.37% and on mainland China, the Shanghai Composite Index lost 1.18%. 
West Texas Intermediate crude rose 0.2% to $63.13 a barrel on Tuesday, after losing 3% on Monday. Gold fell 0.1% to $1,339.70 an ounce after gaining 1.2% If you liked this article you might like
